author: HR5206
title: Save Input overwrites committed deck and wearing-course thicknesses with defaults
body:
## What happened

I saved a 300 mm deck and a 75 mm wearing course in Additional Inputs. Those values remained set until I clicked the main **Save Input** button and saved an OSI. The saved values became 250 mm and 50 mm. In a separate direct-Design run, the intended 300/75 values reached the backend and appeared in the output/report, which helps isolate the save path.

## Environment and reproduction

Windows 11, Python 3.12.16 (conda-forge), `dev` at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3`. The recorder source metadata reports no tracked source modifications. The recorder wraps the original design call; it does not replace the solver.

1. Use span 25 m, carriageway 7.5 m, skew 0°, no median/footpath, Optimized. The attached `T05B_before.osi` contains the complete configuration and custom materials.
2. Open Additional Inputs, set deck thickness to 300 mm and concrete wearing-course thickness to 75 mm, then save that dialog.
3. Click the main Save Input button and save an OSI.
4. Inspect the two thickness keys in the saved file.

| Key | Intended after Additional Inputs Save | Saved OSI |
|---|---:|---:|
| `typical_section.deck_thickness` | 300 | 250 |
| `typical_section.wearing_course.thickness` | 75 | 50 |

Expected: saving preserves validated user inputs. Actual: default expansion overwrites them before serialization.

## Evidence

`T05_save_evidence.zip` contains the original T05B OSI and metadata, plus T05C's successful direct-design inputs, outputs, report and screenshots. T05B contains no design run; I am not presenting it as a completed calculation. The before-save values and action order are my observation, supported by the independent function-level reproduction below; there is no T05B before/after GUI screenshot pair.

The included `reproduce_save_reset.py` loads a copy of the OSI, assigns 300/75 and invokes the same unmodified default-expansion function. Running it against the tested commit produced:

```text
Before: deck_thickness=300.0, wearing_course.thickness=75.0
After:  deck_thickness=250.0, wearing_course.thickness=50.0
AssertionError: Save-path default expansion overwrote custom thicknesses
```

This is a function-level reproduction, not another desktop run. The assertion intentionally fails on the defective version.

## Root cause and suggested fix

[desktop/ui/template_page.py:793](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/template_page.py#L793): `saveOSI_inputs()` invokes `solve_extend_basic_input_dict(self.input_dict)` before opening the save dialog. [core/bridge_types/plate_girder/defaults.py:181](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/defaults.py#L181) uses unconditional `input_dict.update()` for typical-section defaults, including deck thickness 250 and wearing-course thickness 50.

Preserve existing user-editable values when inserting defaults:

```python
def _update(key, value):
    if input_dict.get(key) in (None, ""):
        input_dict[key] = value
```

Separate initial default insertion from derived-layout recomputation and serialization. Saving should serialize the validated state; running the existing destructive helper on a copy alone would still save wrong values. Derived loads and layout must continue to update when their source inputs change. Audit the helper's load and Design callers too.

Regression checks: 300/75 survives save, reload and repeated save; omitted optional values still receive defaults; dependent geometry still updates. Because the call precedes the file dialog, also test cancellation without state mutation. Cancellation is a source-derived risk, not a GUI result I tested. No fix has been applied.

## Duplicate check

I checked open and closed issues on 11 November 2026. #19 concerns custom-material restoration after reload; this issue concerns overwriting additional geometry during Save Input. I found no issue for this exact save/default-expansion defect.

[T05_save_evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34689430/T05_save_evidence.zip)

author: HR5206
title: End Diaphragm tab displays cross-bracing results instead of its own output dictionary
body: ## What happened My design completed and both transverse-member tabs opened. With **G1–G2 / Envelope** selected, the End Diaphragm tab repeated the Crossbracing utilization values. The captured backend dictionaries contain different end-diaphragm results. Windows 11, Python 3.12.16 (conda-forge), `dev` at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3`. The recorder source metadata reports no tracked source modifications. The recorder wraps the original design call; it does not replace the solver. ## Reproduction Span 30 m; carriageway 9 m; skew 10°; Highway Bridge; Chennai (Minambakkam) (A), Tamil Nadu; no median; no footpath; Optimized; deck 300 mm; concrete wearing course 75 mm at 25 kN/m³. Girder `custom_steel_345_500`, cross bracing `custom_steel_275_430`, end diaphragm `custom_steel_355_510`, deck `custom_concrete_45_3.5`. The complete 588-key configuration is in the attached T06 `run_01/input_before.json`. 1. Enter the configuration and save Additional Inputs. Run Design directly, bypassing the separately reported Save Input reset. 2. Open Transverse Member Design, select G1–G2 and Envelope. 3. Compare Crossbracing and End Diaphragm, then compare the end-diaphragm rows with `end_diaphragm_design_results["G1-G2"]`. | Check | Cross-bracing output/UI | End-diaphragm output | End-diaphragm UI | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Diagonal tension | 0.18 | 0.23 | 0.180 | | Diagonal compression | 0.85 | 0.54 | 0.850 | | Chord tension | 0.16 | 0.20 | 0.160 | | Chord compression | 0.74 | 0.47 | 0.740 | The leaf key is `Member.efficiency`, under `diagonal`/`chord` and `tension`/`compression`. Expected: the diaphragm tab displays its own result, with demand, capacity, load case and status belonging to that same component/check. ## Evidence `T06_evidence.zip`: `08_cross_bracing.png`, `09_end_diaphragm.png`, complete input/output dictionaries, runtime/source metadata and report. The successful core call lasted 152.41 seconds; the design's separate structural status is FAIL. This issue is about UI data routing, not whether a failed design may generate CAD. The included `reproduce_ed_merge.py` executes only the actual merge AST extracted from `_try_load_data()` against copies of the captured dictionaries. It reproduces all four substitutions above without Qt or another structural run. Its output is included in the archive. ## Root cause [desktop/ui/dialogs/transverse_member_design.py:920](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/dialogs/transverse_member_design.py#L920) starts with `designs_dict = dict(cb_designs)` and then merges ED entries using `entry.setdefault(k, v)`. Existing `diagonal` and `chord` keys win, leaving CB values in place. Both HTML builders receive the same merged dictionary. `_build_ed_design_check_html()` around line 1412 reads that dictionary; its cross-braced branch around line 1460 also reads the shared force mapping. The outer `dict()` copy is shallow, so adding UI metadata to a nested entry can also modify the backend's CB dictionary. That consequence follows from the source; I did not separately capture the backend after opening the dialog. ## Suggested correction Keep CB and ED results, force records and metadata separate throughout initial load and refresh: ```python from copy import deepcopy self._cb_designs = deepcopy(cb_designs) self._ed_designs = deepcopy(ed_designs) # Add ED metadata only to self._ed_designs. # CB builder: CB force records + self._cb_designs. # ED builder: ED force records + self._ed_designs. ``` Update every builder call, including pair/load-case changes. Replacing `setdefault` with `update` would merely make CB show ED values instead; it is not a correct fix. Do not repair only the UR field while leaving a force from another component beside it. Regression test: distinct CB/ED fixtures must preserve the four ratios above in their own tabs after initialization, tab changes and pair/load-case changes. Opening the dialog must not mutate backend result dictionaries. Proposed fix only; no patched GUI run has been performed. ## Related consistency observation to investigate The same evidence shows G1–G2 CB compression demand/capacity/UR as 9.239 kN / 13.93 kN / 0.85 for the diagonal, and 8.014 / 17.44 / 0.74 for the chord. Dividing the displayed numbers gives approximately 0.663 and 0.460. Report page 40 repeats this mismatch, while page 43 uses a different compression demand, 11.84 kN, consistent with 0.85. The UI builder takes force values from one mapping and efficiency/capacity from another. The report does the same via `get_cb_governing_force()` versus `get_cb_capacity()` / `get_cb_efficiency()` in [core/reports/report_generator.py:540](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/reports/report_generator.py#L540). Preserve the governing check's force, capacity and utilization together, or label a utilization governed by another check explicitly. I have not established that the solver's capacity or efficiency calculation itself is wrong. This observation is related display evidence, not proof that the CB/ED merge is its sole cause. ## Duplicate check Open and closed issues were checked on 11 November 2026. #43 addresses material-property propagation, not the substitution of CB output for distinct ED output. PRs #52 and #55 discuss transverse-module work; this reproduction applies to `dev` at the commit above. I found no existing issue for this exact tab/dictionary mismatch. [T06_evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34689511/T06_evidence.zip)

author: HR5206
title: Girder support-reaction fields disagree with the reaction labels in the same plot
body: ## Reproduction and evidence Windows 11, Python 3.12.16 (conda-forge), `dev` at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3`. The recorder source metadata reports no tracked source modifications. The recorder wraps the original design call; it does not replace the solver. Span 30 m; carriageway 9 m; skew 10°; Highway Bridge; Chennai (Minambakkam) (A), Tamil Nadu; no median; no footpath; Optimized; deck 300 mm; concrete wearing course 75 mm at 25 kN/m³. Girder `custom_steel_345_500`, cross bracing `custom_steel_275_430`, end diaphragm `custom_steel_355_510`, deck `custom_concrete_45_3.5`. The complete 588-key configuration is in the attached T06 `run_01/input_before.json`. After Design, open Girder Analysis and Design Results Summary → Girder 1 → SW → Analysis Results → Major. In `T06_evidence.zip`, `07_plot_a.png` shows: | Location | Left reaction, kN | Right reaction, kN | |---|---:|---:| | Support Reactions fields | 16.31 | 3.42 | | Load sketch labels | 16.3 | 16.7 | The right values differ far beyond rounding. Expected: both displays use the same support-reaction record for the selected member and load case. The design ran and the plot opened; this is a result-display inconsistency rather than a plotting crash. ## Root cause and suggested fix [desktop/ui/dialogs/steel_design.py:947](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/dialogs/steel_design.py#L947) fills `R_A` from `abs(sfd_values[0])` and `R_B` from `abs(sfd_values[-2])`, assuming the penultimate sample is the right-support shear. Later, around line 982, the sketch obtains reactions through `engine.extract_reactions(loadcase, member_key)` instead. [core/bridge_types/plate_girder/graph_engine.py:1061](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/graph_engine.py#L1061) first attempts actual model support reactions, with an SFD-based fallback. This means the field and sketch use different retrieval paths. An SFD sample should not silently stand in for the model reaction. Extract reactions once and share the result between the fields and sketch: ```python reactions = engine.extract_reactions(loadcase, member_key) self._current_max_dict["R_A"] = reactions.get("Ra") self._current_max_dict["R_B"] = reactions.get("Rb") # Pass this same reactions mapping to render_plots(). ``` Handle absent values as unavailable, clearing the previous display. The extractor's fallback also deserves review: select a confirmed support node/component or expose unavailable data rather than assuming the penultimate sample is always a support. Maintain a consistent, documented sign convention. Regression checks should cover straight/skew bridges, changed load cases, component switches and unavailable reaction data. Field and sketch values must agree after rounding. I have not independently calculated the correct reaction or assumed that the sketch is necessarily correct. No patch has been applied. ## Duplicate check Open and closed issues checked on 11 November 2026. #61 concerns Fx/Tx plot titles and #48 concerns report omissions; neither describes these conflicting reaction values. No matching issue found. [T06_evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34689644/T06_evidence.zip)

author: HR5206
title: Runtime deck layout uses a fixed 0.5 m crash-barrier width instead of the input's 0.45 m
body:
## What I found

The design input contains a crash-barrier width of 0.45 m, but the runtime `DeckLayoutProperties` object contains 0.5 m. The mismatch appears in multiple captured designs, including T06. I am reporting input propagation; I have not quantified its effect on final forces or design adequacy.

Windows 11, Python 3.12.16 (conda-forge), `dev` at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3`. The recorder source metadata reports no tracked source modifications. The recorder wraps the original design call; it does not replace the solver.

## Reproduction

Span 30 m; carriageway 9 m; skew 10°; Highway Bridge; Chennai (Minambakkam) (A), Tamil Nadu; no median; no footpath; Optimized; deck 300 mm; concrete wearing course 75 mm at 25 kN/m³. Girder `custom_steel_345_500`, cross bracing `custom_steel_275_430`, end diaphragm `custom_steel_355_510`, deck `custom_concrete_45_3.5`. The complete 588-key configuration is in the attached T06 `run_01/input_before.json`.

Run Design and compare the captured `run_01/input_before.json` with `run_01/runtime_properties.json` in `T06_evidence.zip`:

```text
input_before["typical_section.crash_barrier.width"] = 0.45
input_after["typical_section.crash_barrier.width"]  = 0.45
runtime["deck_layout"]["crash_barrier_width"]      = 0.5
```

Expected: the runtime layout uses the validated width from the input dictionary, unless a documented and explicit transformation applies. Actual: it silently substitutes the fixed default.

## Root cause and proposed change

[core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py:1017](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L1017), `_build_dtos()`, constructs the layout with `crash_barrier_width=float(DEFAULT_CRASH_BARRIER_WIDTH)`. The declared input key `KEY_CB_WIDTH` is `typical_section.crash_barrier.width`.

Read and validate that key instead of substituting the constant. For example, after shared input validation:

```python
raw_width = inp.get(KEY_CB_WIDTH)
if raw_width in (None, ""):
    raise ValueError("Crash-barrier width is required before building the deck layout")
barrier_width = float(raw_width)
# Use barrier_width in DeckLayoutProperties(...).
```

Default initialization, if supported for this field, should happen once before validation and be reflected in the input state. Validation should reject nonfinite/invalid widths and preserve an explicitly supported zero-width/no-barrier case rather than using a truthiness fallback.

Regression check: input 0.45 produces runtime 0.45; a second accepted custom width propagates too; missing/invalid inputs follow the documented validation/default path. Check dependent width/load calculations after the change. This is a proposed fix, not a tested patch.

## Duplicate check

Open and closed issues checked on 11 November 2026. #64 concerns railing line load, while #41 concerns deck material density. Neither covers crash-barrier width in the runtime layout. No matching issue found.

[T06_evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34690296/T06_evidence.zip)

author: HR5206
body:
I reproduced this through the desktop reload path at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` on Windows 11/Python 3.12.16, and found two useful additional symptoms.

The original `T04_source.osi` contains complete custom properties. After loading it in a fresh session, the steel information button raised:

```text
material_properties.py, line 751, _load_material_info_for_view
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'defaults' where it is not associated with a value
```

The deck information dialog opened with the custom name still selected, but fck/fctm/Ecm were blank. Comparing the original OSI with `T04_before.osi` shows exactly five changes:

| Deck key | Source | Re-saved pre-design state |
|---|---:|---:|
| density | 25.5 | 24.5 |
| fck | 45 | null |
| fctm | 3.5 | null |
| ecm | 35 | null |
| thermal | 10.5 | 11.7 |

The selected name stays `custom_concrete_45_3.5`. All other 575 saved key/value pairs are equal. The design attempt in `run_03` then stops with `ValueError: 'material.deck.fck' is required but was not found in 'input_dict'`. Earlier attempts in the same session contain cancellation messages; I am not counting them as crashes.

Evidence is in `T04_evidence.zip`: both OSIs, screenshots, `run_03` dictionaries and the full traceback. Geometry w

[T04_evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34689798/T04_evidence.zip)

as span 25 m, carriageway 7.5 m, skew 0°, no median/footpath, Optimized. Steel was `custom_steel_345_500`; the OSI preserves all exact parameters. This is a dialog callback exception plus a handled design failure, not a confirmed process crash.

In addition to rebuilding the custom-property map in `InputDock.populate_from_dict()`, please handle the missing-map branch in [desktop/ui/dialogs/material_properties.py:751](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/desktop/ui/dialogs/material_properties.py#L751). The name-parsing path can reach `defaults` without initializing it. Initializing that local variable prevents the exception, but does not restore the lost concrete data by itself.

A complete fix should reconstruct per-component property dictionaries from the OSI before info/Save/Additional Inputs/Design can re-prime them. Avoid relying only on a grade name as material identity when two components may share a name but have different values. Preserve complete saved values; reject an incomplete custom material clearly rather than silently filling arbitrary strengths. Tests should exercise a fresh process, all material information dialogs, re-save and a subsequent design. No patch has been applied in my testing.

author: HR5206
body:
Additional runtime evidence from T06 at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3` (Windows 11/Python 3.12.16):

```text
input_before/material.girder.density = 77 kN/m³
input_after/material.girder.density  = 77 kN/m³
output_after/material.girder.density = 77 kN/m³

```

Other custom girder properties do propagate: E = 205e9 Pa, Fy = 345e6 Pa, Fu = 500e6 Pa and Poisson = 0.3. Thus a matching input/output dictionary alone does not establish that the density was used.

Span 30 m; carriageway 9 m; skew 10°; Highway Bridge; Chennai (Minambakkam) (A), Tamil Nadu; no median; no footpath; Optimized; deck 300 mm; concrete wearing course 75 mm at 25 kN/m³. Girder `custom_steel_345_500`, cross bracing `custom_steel_275_430`, end diaphragm `custom_steel_355_510`, deck `custom_concrete_45_3.5`. The complete 588-key configuration is in the attached T06 `run_01/input_before.json`.

The full evidence is in `T06_evidence.zip`, especially `input_before.json`, `output_after.json` and `runtime_properties.json`. The core call returned without an exception; that is separate from its failed fatigue check.

[core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py:1192](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L1192) still substitutes `_DEFAULT_DENSITY` when the database lookup has no result. The proposed custom-key fallback should yield **77000 N/m³** for this 77 kN/m³ input. A regression should also check the resulting self-weight with section and geometry held fixed; comparing optimized runs can otherwise mix density and sizing effects. I have not patched the code or measured that isolated sensitivity here.

author: HR5206
body:
I found a second calculation path affected by custom deck density, in addition to the analysis-load path already described here.

In T05C at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3`, the captured deck density is 25.5 kN/m³ and slab thickness is 300 mm. Both survive the design call, but the deck-design calculation text and report use **7.36 kN/m²** for slab dead load. Using the entered weight density gives **25.5 × 0.300 = 7.65 kN/m²**.

Evidence: `T05_save_evidence.zip`, under `t05c/`, includes the 300 mm input screenshot, complete recorder JSON and `T05C_report.pdf` (physical page 37, including cover). Geometry: span 25 m, carriageway 7.5 m, skew 0°, no median/footpath, Optimized; wearing course Concrete/75 mm; custom concrete `custom_concrete_45_3.5`. All exact parameters are in `input_before.json`.

[core/bridge_types/plate_girder/deckdesign.py:516](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/deckdesign.py#L516) contains:

```python
gamma_concrete_kN_m3 = IRC6_2017.cl_203_dead_load()["concrete_cement_reinforced"] * 9.81
w_DL_kN_m2 = gamma_concrete_kN_m3 * (deck_t_mm / 1000.0)
```

This path reads the code-table value instead of the custom material density. Fixing only `create_deck_load()` would leave this calculation inconsistent.

Please pass the validated concrete weight density into the deck-design function too, using a named argument such as `concrete_weight_density_kN_m3`, and calculate `w_DL_kN_m2 = concrete_weight_density_kN_m3 * deck_t_mm / 1000.0`. The UI already supplies weight density in kN/m³, so it should not receive another gravity conversion. Keep a clearly defined default path only for genuinely unspecified materials.

A focused regression should require 7.65 kN/m² for this configuration and confirm agreement between the global-analysis and deck-design load paths. No patched run has been performed.

[T05_save_evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34689932/T05_save_evidence.zip)

author: HR5206
body:
T06 adds a distinct-material configuration at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3`:

| Component | Grade | Fy/Fu, MPa | E, GPa | Weight density, kN/m³ |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Girder | custom_steel_345_500 | 345/500 | 205 | 77.0 |
| Cross bracing | custom_steel_275_430 | 275/430 | 200 | 77.2 |
| End diaphragm | custom_steel_355_510 | 355/510 | 210 | 78.0 |

All `material.*` keys match between the input-before, input-after and output dictionaries. Runtime `steel_prop` contains the girder values. This supports the retention-versus-use distinction, but I did not capture every internal CLI material object.

There is an additional concrete source path to include in the fix: [core/bridge_types/plate_girder/crossbracingforces.py:608](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/crossbracingforces.py#L608) copies `design_dict_tension_bolted` / `design_dict_struts_bolted` and sets load and length without replacing their component material fields. The cross-braced ED path in [core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py:2759](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/bridge_types/plate_girder/plategirderbridge.py#L2759) follows the same pattern. These templates in [core/utils/connect.py:131](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/utils/connect.py#L131) contain fixed material entries, including `Material` and `Member.Material` values such as `E 250 (Fe 410 W)A`.

Therefore, creating separate global DTOs alone is insufficient: the actual member-design job payloads must receive the validated component material properties in the representation supported by the downstream solver. Passing only an unknown custom name is insufficient if that solver expects a database grade. Connector material selection should remain explicit and separate from member material selection.

`T06_evidence.zip` includes the exact inputs, material-selection screenshot, runtime properties and outputs. Geometry was 30 m span, 9 m carriageway, 10° skew, deck 300 mm and wearing course 75 mm.

Suggested regression: inspect each constructed CB/ED job payload using these distinct properties, then vary only one component's yield strength with section and loads fixed and check that only the appropriate member calculation changes. This is proposed validation, not a sensitivity test I have already run.

[T06_evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34689986/T06_evidence.zip)

author: HR5206
body:
Additional report data-fidelity finding at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3`: T06's material take-off labels the deck **“Concrete (M40)”** even though its selected material is `custom_concrete_45_3.5`, and the input/runtime/design result contain fck = 45 MPa.

This appears on physical page 50 of `T06_report.pdf`. `T06_evidence.zip` includes the original PDF, a rendered page extract `report_page_50.png`, and complete input/output dictionaries. The design configuration is span 30 m, carriageway 9 m, skew 10°, deck 300 mm, wearing course 75 mm, Optimized.

The label is literal text in [core/reports/chap7.py:22](https://github.com/Nidhikhare12/OsdagBridge/blob/d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3/src/osdagbridge/core/reports/chap7.py#L22):

```text
3 & Concrete (M40) for Deck Slab & ...
```

Please generate it from `KEY_DECK_CONCRETE_GRADE_BASIC` (and optionally the numeric fck), using the report's LaTeX escaping helper. For a custom grade, preserve its name or explicitly show fck = 45 MPa; do not silently relabel it as a standard grade. A regression should use a non-M40 grade and assert that the quantity table agrees with the material section. I am reporting the label mismatch, not claiming that all quantity calculations were independently verified.

[T06_evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34690042/T06_evidence.zip)

author: HR5206
body:
I reproduced the contradictory summary with custom materials in T06 at `d74f56dd7f22925fb8148cabf5740ed8d1e39ff3`. Physical page 6 of `T06_report.pdf` shows fatigue utilization **1.89** and then prints **“Girder design pass.”** The captured `design_results.overall_status` is `FAIL`, with `max_dcr = 1.8924` and a failed Fatigue Normal Stress check.
